stem: Per Rule 110101, how is an 'appeal' defined under the PSR?

options.A: A formal request for a pay increase unrelated to any decision
options.B: A request submitted only after resignation from the Service
options.C: A formal request made by an aggrieved Officer for reconsideration of the decision of an appropriate authority
options.D: Any informal complaint raised verbally to a colleague

explanation: Rule 110101: an appeal is a formal request made by an aggrieved Officer for reconsideration of the decision of an appropriate authority.

stem: Per Rule 110101, how does a 'petition' differ from an appeal?

options.A: A petition can only be submitted by a group of at least five officers
options.B: A petition is identical to an appeal in every respect, with no distinction
options.C: A petition is a formal complaint for consideration of a matter affecting the Officer personally or bordering on general/public interest, not necessarily tied to reconsidering a specific decision
options.D: A petition may only be submitted after an appeal has already failed

explanation: Rule 110101: a petition is a formal complaint made by an Officer to an appropriate authority for consideration of a matter affecting the Officer personally or bordering on general/public interest.

stem: Per Rule 110102, which authority should representations relating to appointments, promotion, transfer, and discipline be addressed to?

options.A: The Head of the officer's MDA only
options.C: The Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
options.D: The Chairman, Federal Civil Service Commission

explanation: Rule 110102(a): matters relating to appointments, promotion, transfer and discipline go to the Chairman, Federal Civil Service Commission.

options.B: The Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
options.D: The Chairman, Federal Civil Service Commission

explanation: Rule 110102(b): the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation handles matters relating to other conditions of service such as leave, passages, allowances, pensions, and gratuities.

stem: Per Rule 110103, in what form must a communication to the Head of Government be transmitted through the proper channel?

options.B: Unsealed and in a single copy only
options.C: Sealed and in a single copy

explanation: Rule 110103: the Officer must transmit such communication unsealed and in triplicate to the appropriate channel.

stem: Per Rule 110103, what happens to a letter or document received by the Head of Government otherwise than through the proper channel?

options.A: It is forwarded directly to the National Assembly
options.B: It is destroyed without further notice
options.C: It is automatically actioned with top priority
options.D: It will be returned to the writer

explanation: Rule 110103: every letter or document received by the Head of Government otherwise than through the proper channel will be returned to the writer.

stem: Per Rule 110201, within how long must an appeal from an aggrieved Officer be handled and concluded?
explanation: Rule 110201(i): appeal from an aggrieved Officer shall be handled and concluded within six months.

stem: Per Rule 110201, before proceeding to court, what must an Officer generally do first?

options.A: Obtain permission from the National Assembly
options.B: Nothing further -- Officers may proceed directly to court at any time with no prior steps
options.C: Exhaust all avenues provided in the Public Service Rules and Circulars for redress, and obtain the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation's permission

explanation: Rule 110201(ii): Officers should exhaust all avenues provided in the PSR and Circulars for redress before proceeding to courts, and must also obtain the permission of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation before proceeding to court.

stem: Per Rule 110203, what is the proper first course of action for an Officer who is dissatisfied with a decision, consistent with the prohibition on outside influence?

options.A: To submit the matter directly to the President
options.B: To make representation to his immediate superior Officer or Permanent Secretary/Head of Extra-Ministerial Office
options.C: To seek the personal intervention of a prominent public figure
options.D: To publicize the grievance in the press

explanation: Rule 110203: if dissatisfied, the proper course is to make representation to his immediate superior Officer or Permanent Secretary/Head of Extra-Ministerial Office.

stem: Per Rule 110204, through whom must an appeal/petition be submitted, before it reaches the Chairman of the FCSC or the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation?

options.B: The petitioner's immediate superior Officer and the Permanent Secretary/Head of Extra-Ministerial Office
options.C: Only the officer's own labour union representative
options.D: No intermediate channel is required -- petitions go directly to the final authority

explanation: Rule 110204: an appeal/petition must be submitted through the proper departmental channels -- the petitioner's immediate superior Officer and the Permanent Secretary/Head of Extra-Ministerial Office, who forward it with comments and recommendations.

stem: Per Rule 110205, in how many copies must an appeal/petition addressed to the appropriate channels be submitted?
explanation: Rule 110205: an appeal/petition must be submitted in duplicate, with one copy retained by the Permanent Secretary/Head of Extra-Ministerial Office.

options.B: Only the petitioner's staff number, with no other identifying information
options.C: The signature of the petitioner's immediate superior only, not the petitioner's own

stem: Per Rule 110207, when a person submits a petition on behalf of an illiterate person, what must the petition contain?

options.C: The signature of a court-appointed guardian only
options.D: A statement that the writer has been asked to write on behalf of the illiterate person

stem: Per Rule 110208, will an appeal/petition be entertained if it deals with a case in which legal action is pending in a Court of Law?

options.B: Yes, provided the officer withdraws the court case within thirty days
options.C: Only if the Federal Civil Service Commission grants special dispensation
options.D: Yes, pending legal action has no bearing on whether a petition is entertained

explanation: Rule 110208(a)(ii): an appeal/petition will not be entertained if it deals with a case in which legal action is pending in a Court of Law.

options.B: No, under no circumstances, even with new relevant matter
options.C: Yes, provided it is resubmitted within thirty days of the original
options.D: Yes, repetition alone is never grounds for rejection

explanation: Rule 110208(a)(v): a petition which merely repeats the substance of a previous petition without introducing new relevant matter will not be entertained.

stem: Per Rule 110209, an appeal/petition submitted more than how long after the decision complained of will not be entertained, unless supported by valid reasons?
explanation: Rule 110209: an appeal/petition submitted more than six months after the decision complained of will not be entertained, unless such delay is supported by valid reasons.
